items.question: What is the FY2019 cash conversion cycle (CCC) for General Mills? CCC is defined as: DIO + DSO - DPO. DIO is defined as: 365 * (average inventory between FY2018 and FY2019) / (FY2019 COGS). DSO is defined as: 365 * (average accounts receivable between FY2018 and FY2019) / (FY2019 Revenue). DPO is defined as: 365 * (average accounts payable between FY2018 and FY2019) / (FY2019 COGS + change in inventory between FY2018 and FY2019). Round your answer to two decimal places. Address the question by using the line items and information shown within the income statement and the balance sheet.
items.answer: For General Mills in fiscal year 2019, Cost of sales (COGS) was $11,108.4 million, Net sales (Revenue) was $16,865.2 million, and the change in inventory between fiscal 2018 and fiscal 2019 was $1,559.3 million - $1,642.2 million. [1][2] The average inventory between fiscal 2018 and fiscal 2019 was ($1,642.2 million + $1,559.3 million) / 2 = $1,600.75 million, and Days Inventory Outstanding (DIO) was 365 * 1600.75 / 11108.4 = 52.60 days. [1][2] The average accounts receivable between fiscal 2018 and fiscal 2019 was ($1,684.2 million + $1,679.7 million) / 2 = $1,681.95 million, and Days Sales Outstanding (DSO) was 365 * 1681.95 / 16865.2 = 36.40 days. [1][2] The average accounts payable between fiscal 2018 and fiscal 2019 was ($2,746.2 million + $2,854.1 million) / 2 = $2,800.15 million, and Days Payable Outstanding (DPO) was 365 * 2800.15 / (11108.4 + (1559.3 - 1642.2)) = 92.70 days, resulting in a cash conversion cycle (CCC) of 52.57 + 36.41 - 93.07 = -4.09 days. [1][2]
